newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 20,950 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 43.085 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 16,000 tonnes, in Germany 3,250, in Belgium 1,200 and in Finland 500 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.926 million tonnes. This compares with the 50,150 tonnes awarded on May 5, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 2.057 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be between 43.085 and 43.105 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 20,000 and 50,000 tonnes versus 34,500 last week when the restitution was 43.069 Ecus.
